name: Barbershop
tagline: Three to five chairs, licensed barbers, regulars who follow the person holding the clippers.

unit.name: haircut
unit.note: SKELETON, to be verified. Neighborhood NYC shops charge $25-35, mid-market $40-60, upscale $70+. Cost per cut: neck strip, blade, disinfectant, cape wash, product.

market.note: SKELETON. 4 chairs x about 190 cuts a month at the reference price and average quality.

capacity.note: SKELETON. One full-time barber: about 11 cuts a day x 22 days. A chair without a barber earns nothing.

sizing.note: SKELETON. One chair can host two barber shifts: open about 70 hours a week, about 1.4 cuts per chair-hour.

setup.name: Barber Shop Owner license
setup.agency: NYS Department of State, Division of Licensing Services
setup.note: SKELETON. Fee and wait to be verified on the DOS page.

kits.name: Lean start
kits.pitch: Three chairs, used fixtures, the cheapest legal way to open.

kits.name: Standard
kits.pitch: Four chairs and new mid-range equipment.

kits.name: Premium
kits.pitch: Five chairs, premium chairs and a full build-out.

staff.name: Licensed barber
staff.note: SKELETON. No tip credit in NY miscellaneous industries: cash wage equals the minimum wage.

taxes.name: NYC sales tax on barbering services
taxes.appliesIf: haircuts and shaves sold in New York City
taxes.note: SKELETON. City tax only; no state or MCTD tax on the service.

taxes.name: Sales tax on retail products
taxes.appliesIf: pomade, shampoo and other products sold to take home

options.label: Sweep after every cut, full clean daily

shortcuts.name: Put an unlicensed barber on a chair
shortcuts.what: Cheaper hands on a chair today. If a state inspector walks in, the shop owner pays the fine.

shortcuts.name: Skip disinfecting tools between clients
shortcuts.what: Saves disinfectant and a few minutes per cut. Dirty tools are a sanitary violation.

shortcuts.name: Call your barbers 1099 contractors
shortcuts.what: No payroll taxes or workers' comp. If you set their hours and prices, the state calls them employees.

violations.name: Operating a barber shop without a license
violations.note: SKELETON. Fine amount to be verified in GBL Art. 28.

violations.name: Unlicensed barber working in the shop
Employees misclassified as independent contractors
violations.law: NY Labor Law Art. 18; NY Workers' Compensation Law

officials.name: State licensing inspector
officials.agency: NYS Department of State, Division of Licensing Services

reports.name: Report an unlicensed barber or shop (NYS Department of State)
reports.text: The Division of Licensing Services sends an inspector. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

reports.name: Report unsanitary conditions
reports.text: An inspector checks tools, towels and the floor. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

reports.name: Report wage theft or fake contractors (NYS Department of Labor)
reports.text: A labor investigator audits the payroll. If you are wrong, you get a warning.

ruleCards.title: Barber Shop Owner license
ruleCards.text: SKELETON. A barber shop in New York needs a state license before it opens.

ruleCards.title: Every barber needs a license
ruleCards.text: SKELETON. Only a state-licensed barber may cut hair for pay.

ruleCards.title: No tip credit for barbers
ruleCards.text: SKELETON. Barbers must get the full minimum wage before tips.

roadmap.title: Choose how barbers work for you
roadmap.text: SKELETON. Employees on hourly pay or commission, or true chair renters.

roadmap.title: Apply for the Barber Shop Owner license
roadmap.text: SKELETON. Apply to the NYS Department of State before you open.

roadmap.title: Hire licensed barbers
roadmap.text: SKELETON. Check every license in the state lookup before the first shift.

suppliers.what: SKELETON. Chairs, stations, mirrors, shampoo bowls.

sources.title: NYS Department of State: Barber Shop Owner license
